obligations.obligation: must_include: The contract taken at the board for the three stated reasons (pay; Teague's crew on the hold contracts; Cael wanting ground, not teeth — paid to catalogue for the first time).
obligations.evidence: The slip read at the plank on the seventieth day and the three reasons counted in order. Pay: 'It paid. Seventy marks was the ford's price and three-quarters again, for a walk.' Teague's crew: 'Teague's crew was gone on the hold contracts, a week out and a week back, and Oxhollow's slip had come in on a carter behind them and sat four days on the plank with nobody's finger on it.' Ground, not teeth: 'And the third reason, which he counted last because it was his: it was ground. Not teeth.' / 'He had never once been paid to catalogue.' The take: '"That one," he said.' and Seln moving the slip a quarter-inch. No contact with Teague's crew: they are gone before the chapter opens and are mentioned only as an absence.

obligations.obligation: must_include: The freedom movement rendered as scene and cataloguing, not summary: high country, the gorge opening below, each companion at their competence (Karis mapping; Lira running the bench; Brom and the cart; Seln and the campsites), Cael logging at every halt. Injuries carried (taped ankle, bound forearm, the calf, the scarred hands).
obligations.evidence: The bench and gorge catalogued in scene: 'The bench, when they reached it, was a shelf.' / 'On the right the shelf stopped, and past where it stopped there was nothing for a long way down, and at the bottom of the nothing a white line that was a river.' Four companion paragraphs each opening on the competence: 'Lira went ahead.' ('Shale that held a walker held nothing, she said; shale that held a runner held a wheel.'); 'Karis mapped.' (cord, stride count, pitch, dropped stone, 'a line, kinked, with figures along it'); 'Brom kept the cart on the mountain.' ('a cart on scree did not roll; it floated.'); 'Seln was ahead of Lira.' ('"Here," he said, which was the whole report.'); 'Cael wrote.' at every halt. Injuries carried on the page: the yard inventory (calf 'Uphill it still said nine'; Brom's forearm 'bound wrist to elbow still ... The hand was allowed to hold. It was not allowed to pull.'; Lira's taping described in full; Karis's palms 'two lines across each palm, pink and raised'), then on the mountain: 'the calf said nine the entire way', Lira taping at the fan's foot and at every night's fire, Brom's bound arm inside the shaft, Karis's 'scarred hand'/'scarred finger'.

obligations.obligation: must_include: Shale-backs taught before they matter: seen at distance (thirty, armored, placid, the size of carts, grazing lichen); Pike's rule via Seln verbatim; Karis's day-long observation and derivation (unit movement; flight from declarations; 'on a slope, flight is a landslide with legs'). No stampede occurs.
obligations.evidence: Seen at distance on the second day, two hundred meters up, counted three times and kept at thirty: 'got twenty-nine and then thirty-one and then thirty, and kept thirty.'; armored ('Plated across the back in slabs that overlapped like the stone of a roof'), cart-sized ('the size of the cart with its load and Brom in the shafts'), grazing lichen, placid ('Placid was Pike's word for them, by Seln's report, and from below it was the word'). Pike's rule verbatim through Seln: '"Never be below them. Never be *loud* below them."' (and repeated without emphasis on Karis's request). Karis's day: spacing, unit drift, sound and a rock doing nothing ('That's not flight. That's a step.'), then the plate slip and the whole herd moving uphill one length at once ('They moved as a unit. Away.'); the derivation against the ford page ('The herd's answer is the ford's answer with the sign changed: a hunter comes to it; a grazer goes from it. Flight, not hunt.'), the direction ('If the loud thing is below them—' / 'They go up' / 'And if it's *above* them.' / 'Then they come down.'), and the line: '"On a slope, flight is a landslide with legs."' Entered as derived, not tested. No stampede: the herd's only movement is one body's length uphill, then grazing; it is above and behind the party at the close.

obligations.obligation: must_include: The fourth-night log entry (content as in scene_shape) mid-chapter.
obligations.evidence: Fourth camp entry, seventy-sixth day: '*The traverse holds. So far. The map's good — Karis's, not mine; mine's the check. The herd's above the eighth narrowing tonight, thirty, grazing along. Karis says they go off declarations, as a unit, away, and on a slope away is down; which means the loudest thing on this mountain is us, and we've been quiet four days. Not one of us has had to try.*' and 'First honest job I've ever had that didn't have a fight at the end of it. I'm writing that before it's finished, which I don't do. Note that I did.*' The sentence is written on the fourth night and written again on the fifth, which is the chapter's rendering of 'choosing to believe the job has no teeth'.

obligations.obligation: must_include: The chapter ENDS on the fifth-night image-then-log exactly as in closing_state — Lira taping the ankle and announcing the ledge; the final words are Cael's entry ending 'Sleep.'
obligations.evidence: Image: Lira at the fire taping the ankle ('It was the ankle that had never been seen by anyone who could do more for it than boil the cloth.'), then '"I'll run it at first light," she said. "See if it holds a cart."' Then 'He took the log out.' and the final lines of the file: '*The traverse holds. The map's good. Karis says the herd moves off declarations, which means the loudest thing on this mountain is us, and we've been quiet for five days. One more day. First honest job I've ever had that didn't have a fight at the end of it. Sleep.*' — verbatim to closing_state, the last line of prose, no metadata after it.

obligations.obligation: must_include: Cael's cataloguing at scale (a map, a bench, a herd) outside the log at least once; the three boxes in the cart glimpsed once (load-bearing in Chapter 6).
obligations.evidence: Outside the log: the fan catalogued from the bottom; the bench catalogued ('He wrote that down first, at the first halt, because it was the fact everything else stood on.'); the herd counted as a crowd is counted; the narrowings numbered one through nine with widths; the two-thirds count on the tail-board on the fifth night. The three boxes: roped on at Lowmarch ('the front box over the axle and the other two behind it'), re-roped by Brom at every halt, and glimpsed in scene on Karis's day: 'The three boxes rode roped at its front, the foremost over the axle where Brom kept it, the middle one with a corner worn white where the rope ran'.

obligations.obligation: must_include: Manuscript format: H1 '# Chapter 5 — Route', prose only, '---' breaks, ends on the last line of prose.
obligations.evidence: First line is '# Chapter 5 — Route'; eleven '---' breaks; no headings, notes, or counts; the file ends on the log entry's 'Sleep.'

obligations.obligation: plant: Shale-backs flee declarations as a unit; below them is the wrong place to be loud (Chapter 6's engine).
obligations.evidence: Karis's derivation in scene ('They moved as a unit. Away.' / 'Away from the declaration.' / 'Then they come down.' / 'On a slope, flight is a landslide with legs.'), plus Cael's arithmetic on the rule: 'The first half was a carter's wish. The second half was the job.' and the second-camp log: 'We are below them. Every cart Oxhollow ever sends will be below them. So the rule out here is the second half'.

obligations.obligation: plant: The ledge over the gorge that Lira will run at first light (Chapter 6 opens there).
obligations.evidence: 'The fifth day showed them the ledge.' — the bench 'pinching down to a lip that was, at that distance, a line. A ledge.', the herd 'above them and ... behind them now', Karis unable to measure it from the camp, and Lira's announcement at the fire, restated in the final log's dateline: 'The ledge is in sight; Lira runs it at first light.'

obligations.obligation: plant: The three boxes riding in the cart (Chapter 6 costs the cart).
obligations.evidence: Boxes roped on at Lowmarch because there is nowhere to leave them, Brom re-roping them at every halt to keep the weight over the axle, and the middle box opened for the ford page on Karis's day.

obligations.obligation: plant: Lira's ankle, never seen by a healer (Chapter 6).

obligations.obligation: plant: Oxhollow as a ford settlement on the route (Oryn's route, Chapter 7).
obligations.evidence: Named on the slip ('Oxhollow ford') and held to the packet's boundary: 'Oxhollow was a ford, north, a week by the void road; that was the whole of what the plank knew about it.' Payment is at Oxhollow; the bench 'went on toward Oxhollow'. Nobody from Oxhollow appears; no other fact about it is asserted.

obligations.obligation: payoff: Chapter 4's want-lines lived: Lira running, Brom holding, Karis mapping, Seln scouting — each priced by what they do.
obligations.evidence: Lira: runs the bench without Wind ('not a burst; a burst was a shout') and prices herself at the fire: '"That's what I'm for up here. That's the job.' Brom: holds the cart with his body and the strap, the bound arm inside the shaft ('a lock somebody else had built, being held shut by hand'). Karis: the map is hers ('The map's good — Karis's, not mine; mine's the check') and the herd is her first primary source ('First primary source I've had on this side of the Line. It's got a hundred and twenty legs and it doesn't know I'm here.'). Seln: asks Pike about the shale-backs unasked, finds every camp before anyone knows they need one, and reports in one word.

obligations.obligation: payoff: Chapter 3's stillhound sense rhymed and inverted by the shale-backs (Karis names the rhyme).
obligations.evidence: Karis has the ford page read aloud and names it: 'Those turn as one to the loudest thing and then follow the first to go. These go as one and there's no first. Same shape, upside down.' and 'The herd senses discharge — the ford's sense.' — the same sense, the opposite response, in her method-register, entered as derived.

obligations.obligation: prohibited_outcomes (all): no collapse/stampede/fight/new injury; no fragment use or declaration by anyone; no Oryn/healer/Tide/quiet ground beyond one passing thought; no Teague contact, letters, Vastin, watchers; no new named people or places; ends on the log, not dialogue or image; no modern idiom, no feeling/growth declarations, tic caps, no metadata.
obligations.evidence: No ledge collapse (the ledge is only seen), no stampede (the herd moves one body's length), no fight, no new injury. Nobody declares; Cael's log records 'Nothing drifting' and 'Nothing's drifted in four days'; Lira runs without a burst; Karis refuses any trial. No healer, Tide, or Oryn; quiet ground appears as one passing thought only: 'There was a rumor with two lines under it in that box too, near the bottom, and she did not take it out.' Teague's crew is absent for the whole chapter; no letters, Vastin, or watchers. New proper nouns: none (Oxhollow was pre-authorized; the bench, gorge, fan, ledge, and traverse are descriptive). Ends on the log entry. Tic greps all zero; no modern registers; no feeling or growth declarations.

inventions: The Oxhollow slip's wording and price: seventy marks on the map, paid at Oxhollow; the traverse reckoned by Pike at seven or eight days for a cart; the slide dated 'three seasons' ago and placed on the Thornwater end, a mile short of the steading, with a knocked-over cairn where the traverse leaves the road. Oxhollow itself held to 'a ford, north, a week by the void road' and nothing more.

Board state on the seventieth day: thirteen slips, two of them HOLD/Teague hold contracts; Teague's crew came in off the autumn road and went out again with the hold slips while the five were at the well on the south road (Seln's Chapter 4 slip), so there is no contact and no look exchanged. Pike's pricing of why nobody had taken the slip ('Pays on the map, at Oxhollow ... the crews that could take it are the crews with the pick').

The cart: a smith's second-best two-wheeled hand-cart with shafts and a chest-strap, hired for six marks against its return on Pike's instruction ('You want to tell a ford it holds a cart, you'd better have had one on it'); Brom in the shafts with the bound arm inside the right shaft. The boxes go because Lowmarch has no wall and no warehouse and nothing left in a meadow stays.

Pike telling Seln, privately, to ask him about the shale-backs; Seln asking with his back to the room; Cael deliberately not going to hear it — so that Pike's rule arrives on the mountain in Seln's mouth, verbatim, twice.

Injury texture at three weeks: Cael's flat-ground count abandoned past twenty ('a number that large was not a limp, it was a leg'), uphill still nine; Brom's wrist closed on the sixty-sixth day and re-wrapped anyway, the hand allowed to hold but not pull; Lira's stick abandoned on the sixty-fourth day and Pike standing it behind the plank; Lira's taping method in full (boiled-linen strips from the arch over the joint to the shin, morning and, on the mountain, night); Karis's palms as two raised pink lines she flexes against the pen.

Mountain detail: the fan as a field-wide spill of loose plates hauled up on a rope in a morning; the bench as a roof-pitched shelf a cart and a half wide with an upper bench two hundred meters above; the gorge that gives every sound back late from the far wall ('It was the loudest thing about the place, that it repeated you'); the shale-backs' grinding heard before they are seen; overhang camps; nine numbered narrowings with widths (a cart and a hand at the fourth, a clean break at the eighth); the ledge sighted from the ninth.

Karis's mapping method (stride paced against the folding rule, cord widths, pitch by cord and stone, gorge depth by dropped-stone count, 'a line, kinked, with figures along it'); Brom's scree mechanics ('a cart on scree did not roll; it floated', weight over the axle and up-slope, himself on the down-slope shaft as counter); Lira's rule ('shale that held a walker held nothing; shale that held a runner held a wheel') and her hundreds.

Karis's day of observation as a sequence of trials with results: spacing (never closer than a body, never further than three), the line moving without any animal seen to move, a tail-board bang and a falling rock producing only a step, and one plate tilting under an edge animal — the herd taking one body's length uphill at the same instant with no leader. The derivation is built only from that, the ford page (read aloud by Cael from the page in his hand), and the carters' word 'loud'; she enters it as derived and refuses any test.
Marks arithmetic in the first log: sixty-two earned (Chapter 4's fifty-eight plus the four-mark well), forty-six in hand after the cart's six.

Cael's log lines on idle drift stopping on the mountain ('Anchor wanted the inn door; there is no door up here' / 'Nothing's drifted in four days. I'm writing that as a fact and not as a meaning') and on being 'paid by the line' — both kept as observations, not meanings.
Karis's dry line for her want: 'First primary source I've had on this side of the Line. It's got a hundred and twenty legs and it doesn't know I'm here.'
state_change_proposals: Timeline: the Oxhollow slip is read and taken at Lowmarch's board on the SEVENTIETH day past the Line; the five leave with the cart on the seventy-first; two days up the Thornwater road to the slide's fan (the stretch walked quiet at noon; Thornwater's gate not entered); the fan climbed and the bench reached on the seventy-third (first camp, three narrowings); herd seen on the seventy-fourth (second camp, five narrowings); Karis's observation day the seventy-fifth at the second camp; the seventy-sixth to the fourth camp (eight narrowings); the seventy-seventh to the fifth camp at the ninth narrowing with the ledge in sight. Chapter ends on the night of the seventy-seventh day. Cael is eighteen (stated in the first log).

Cael: nine fragments + anomaly, unchanged; NO deployment this chapter; the log records no idle drift on the mountain ('Nothing drifting' / 'Nothing's drifted in four days', kept as fact). Shadow-adjacent unused. Injury: right calf mostly closed — no count on the flat ('past twenty ... it was a leg'), still nine paces uphill, and the whole fan and every climb 'said nine'; still no healer; nobody has mentioned it. Marks: sixty-two earned, forty-six in hand after six for the cart (the well's four marks assumed collected between Ch4 and Ch5). Four log entries written on the traverse (73rd, 74th, 76th, 77th days). He has written the 'first honest job' sentence twice, before the job is finished, and noted that he did.

Brom: right forearm still bound wrist to elbow; the wrist closed on the sixty-sixth day and he re-wrapped it; the hand may hold, not pull. Pulls the hired cart by chest-strap with the bound arm inside the right shaft and the good hand on the left; re-ropes the boxes at every halt; took the cart across the eighth narrowing's clean break with the down-slope wheel a hand from the edge. Strap off only at the fifth-night fire.

Lira: right ankle stiff ('less than the other, and later'), stick abandoned on the sixty-fourth day (Pike keeps it behind the plank), taped each morning and, on the mountain, each night with boiled-linen strips; never seen by a healer. Ran the bench in hundreds every day without Wind (no burst; 'a burst was a shout'); sat out Karis's observation day on the cart's tail; has announced she will run the ledge at first light to see if it holds a cart.

Karis: palms healed to two raised pink scars each; handwriting back to size; holds the pen normally. Has mapped nine narrowings with widths, pitches, and a drawn break at the eighth — the map is hers and is 'good' by Cael's check; two-thirds of the traverse mapped by Pike's day-count. Has the shale-back finding entered as DERIVED (unit movement, flight from declarations, 'on a slope, flight is a landslide with legs'), with the ford page filed inside the day's page and the same finding written in Cael's book at her request. The quiet-ground rumor remains untouched in the middle box. The three boxes are on the cart, the front one over the axle.

Seln: uninjured; asked Pike about the shale-backs privately; carried Pike's rule to the mountain verbatim; found every camp (overhangs) before it was needed; supplied 'Then they come down.' Seln's Chapter 4 well: assumed walked and cleared for four marks between chapters (stated only through the marks arithmetic and 'at the well on the south road').

The herd: thirty shale-backs on the upper bench, ~two hundred meters above the route; drifted along with the lichen at roughly the cart's pace for four days; at chapter end they are above and, for the first time, BEHIND the party by about half a day's grazing, on the far side of the shoulder the ledge lies beyond. No declaration has been made near them. Their only observed movement is one body's length uphill, as a unit, when a plate slipped under one of them.

The route: the traverse leaves the Thornwater road at a cairn a mile below the steading, up the slide's fan; the lower bench is a shelf a cart and a half wide at its widest, roof-pitched toward the gorge; nine narrowings passed (fourth: a cart and a hand, edge crumbling; eighth: a cart exactly, outer edge a clean break); the ledge ahead pinches to 'a line' where the mountain bulges over the gorge; beyond it the bench widens toward Oxhollow. Pike reckons seven or eight cart-days; five walked.

Board/ledger: the Oxhollow slip entered by Pike under the five names on the seventieth day; payment (seventy marks) due at Oxhollow on delivery of the map; the hired cart (six marks) owed back to Lowmarch's smith. Teague's crew out on two hold contracts, no contact, still eleven up. Known to the party: Pike's rule verbatim; the shale-backs' appearance, placidity, grazing, cohesion; and Karis's DERIVED (not tested) finding that they flee declarations as a unit and would come downhill from a declaration above them.

Tic ledger for Chapter 5: all §9 capped phrases 0; 'the way X [verb]' simile construction 0; single-word paragraphs 0; banned modern registers 0; 'heard about it later' family 0; em dashes 23 in ~5,235 words; 'at the pitch of' register phrase 3 (plus one literal 'pitch of a roof'). Scene-closer: log entry (Ch4 closed on dialogue; no repeat).
deviations: Word count 5,235 against a 4,600 target — inside the 15% tolerance (ceiling 5,290) but above target, in line with Chapters 1–4 (5,269 / 5,169 / 5,150 / 5,273). The first pass ran to ~6,400 and was cut by density in three passes; every mandated beat, both log entries, the verbatim rule, the derivation line, and the exact ending are intact. Further compression toward 4,600 is available in the board section, the yard inventory, and the companion-competence paragraphs without touching obligations.

The 'First honest job I've ever had that didn't have a fight at the end of it' sentence appears twice by design: the scene_shape assigns it to the fourth-night entry and the closing_state to the fifth. The fourth-night entry adds 'I'm writing that before it's finished, which I don't do. Note that I did.' so the repetition reads as Cael choosing to believe the job has no teeth; the fifth-night entry is verbatim to closing_state.

The scouting party walks the traverse from the Thornwater end toward Oxhollow (the fan is on the Thornwater end where the slide came down; payment is at Oxhollow). This is a choice the card leaves open; it was made so that Chapter 6's 'overdue on the traverse' and Chapter 7's four-day walk down to Oxhollow are geographically coherent. The editor may prefer the opposite direction; only the fan's placement and 'toward Oxhollow' would need changing.

A hired hand-cart (no mule) is used so that Chapter 6 can lose the cart into the gorge without an unaccounted animal. The cart's origin (Lowmarch's smith, six marks against return) is invented within the 'cart's mechanics' latitude and is reported here for the ledger.

The interval between Chapter 4 (day 60) and the board (day 70) is compressed into two clauses (the well on the south road; Teague's crew in and out). Seln's four-mark well is assumed done in that gap and appears only in the marks arithmetic; if the editor prefers the well left open, the log's 'Sixty-two earned. Forty-six in hand' becomes fifty-eight / forty-two.

Pike's word 'placid' is attributed to him through Seln's report ('Placid was Pike's word for them, by Seln's report') — a small extension of the off-page conversation the card licenses ('Ask me about the shale-backs before you go').

'Karis, who has never seen a large animal she did not want to document' is rendered by behavior (the day requested and spent; 'First primary source ... a hundred and twenty legs') rather than stated by narration.
